_doc: The sheriff on the road: the script for the voiced lines (#807, #832). One file per mission; its artifact page (the listening board) is built from it, so add takes, casting and new lines here and republish the page. Each line: id, scene, speaker (a cast id), trigger (what in the game makes him say it), when (a branch: the band of his blood loss, sheriff.care, the player's nod or shake), condition, delivery (one line for the voice), words (wordings; a line that can play twice has two or three), setups (SETUPS.md ids it plants or pays), check (a WORDS.md worry). Each wording's status: built = in config/moments/the_sheriff.json now, fixed (not changed here); new = written for this script; bible = a P·bible sample line from docs/story/VOICES.md, used as written or nearly. A wording of '...' is a breath, not words: voiced as a sound. takes: empty until the casting and takes session (3-4 per line). Nothing here is approved until Sean taps Script OK. cast[].voice (#836): design = how the candidates were made (fal's ElevenLabs Voice Design, eleven_ttv_v3: the prompt, the text, guidance; each candidate's seed remakes it); candidates = [{id, url (the page's asset), voice_id (saved on fal's ElevenLabs account), seed}]; picked = the candidate Sean chose (cast/<id>.pick on the page), then fixed; takes_model = the model and settings the takes use.
title: The sheriff on the road
status: draft: waiting on Sean's Script OK
sources: docs/story/OUTLINE.md Act I, VOICES.md (the sheriff, the doctor, the widow, smaller voices), SETUPS.md, WORDS.md (PR #833)
#807 (the pipeline; the artifact page, Sean 2026-11-12), #830 (C12 a: the county sheriff, the doctor as coroner; C14 c: roles only)
notes: Harlan doesn't speak in this mission: he answers by nod and shake and by what he does (VOICES.md).
Roles only (C14 c): Sheriff, Doc, ma'am, Harlan. Nobody names the Baron; the sheriff says 'he'.
The game says a beat's wordings in order and repeats the last (Act.line): once there are takes, the idle and ask-again lines should cycle instead (a gameplay change, later).
Scenes 3 to 5 aren't built yet: their triggers say what they'll need. The built mission ends at the doctor's lot (scene 2) or the freighter's card (scene 3).

WORDS.md: reads as 20th-century ring slang. A period way: 'He's insensible.'
WORDS.md: 'hold it' for 'stop', to check. A period way: 'Hold on there!' or 'Stand!'

cast.name: The sheriff
cast.brief: Mid-fifties, a plains man (Missouri or Kansas, not stage Texas), fourteen years on a Colorado claim. Low and dry, gravel from pain; gives orders even on his back; short sentences that shorten to a word as he bleeds.

design.prompt: A man in his mid-fifties from the American plains, Missouri or Kansas, not a Texas drawl, who has worked a Colorado claim for fourteen years in the 1880s. A low, dry, weathered voice with gravel in it from pain; gut-shot and breathing hard, but still giving orders. Short, plain sentences at an unhurried pace. Natural and close, unpolished, never an announcer's polish.
design.text: [hurt, bitter, breathing hard] Man in a faded red shirt. Rode up easy, like he wanted directions. Then he shot me. [dying, very weak, fading, long pauses] Badge... Doc. Pin it on him.

cast.name: The doctor
cast.bible: VOICES.md, The doctor; WORDS.md, The doctor
cast.brief: Late forties, an educated Easterner gone west (Philadelphia or New England). Brisk, quiet, dry; whole sentences, never raised; counts things.

design.prompt: A man in his late forties, an educated Easterner from Philadelphia who went west to a Colorado town in the 1880s. Brisk, quiet and dry; precise whole sentences, never raised; a clear mid-low voice, a little tired, with a faint old Philadelphia accent. Natural and close, not theatrical.
design.text: [calm, approving] Somebody packed that wound, and packed it right. That's bought him some hours. Come back tonight. [tired, plain] The ball's in the bowel. I can't get at it, and it would make no odds if I could. He'll not see another night.

cast.name: The sheriff's wife
cast.bible: VOICES.md, The widow; WORDS.md, The town's women
cast.brief: About forty, a Midwestern farm wife with good schooling. Level and low, short; grief held under work; asks hard questions plainly.

design.prompt: A woman of about forty, a Midwestern farm wife with good schooling, living in 1880s Colorado. A level, low, plain-spoken alto; grief held down under work; short sentences, hard questions asked plainly. Warm underneath but tired and unadorned. Natural and close.
design.text: [grief held down] Were you with him? [cold] A freighter brought him, they tell me. [grief held down, steady] I'll sit with him now. Go on, the both of you.

cast.name: The freighter
cast.brief: Forties, a teamster, hoarse from shouting at mules; rough country voice, quick, still shaken by what he hauled in.

design.prompt: A man in his forties, a teamster driving freight wagons in 1880s Colorado; a voice hoarse and rough from shouting at mules all day. A rough rural Western country voice, talking quickly, still shaken by the wounded man he hauled into town. Natural and unpolished.
design.text: [shaken, quick] Found him in the road east of the ford. Talked about a red shirt the whole way in. [shaken] Red shirt, he kept saying. Red shirt, and a name. Harlan, or near it.

cast.name: The livery man
cast.brief: Sixties, slow and grumbling to hide that he minds; a little nasal, rural.

design.prompt: A man in his sixties who keeps the livery stable in an 1880s Colorado town; a slow, grumbling, slightly nasal rural voice, gruff to hide that he minds. Unhurried and plain. Natural and unpolished.
design.text: [shaken, grumbling] That's the sheriff's bay. Lord. I'll put him up. Saddle, rifle and all. [grumbling] Leave him with me. I'll see he's fed, whoever's paying.

scenes.title: The road
scenes.when: Day 1, dawn, the East Road where the ford path meets it (opening_site)
scenes.setting: Harlan walks down from his homestead and finds the sheriff shot through the belly, his horse standing off the road with its reins down. What the sheriff says is chosen by how much blood he's lost: clear, weak or fading.

lines.speaker: sheriff
lines.trigger: You come within 25 m of him (hail_m)
lines.delivery: Up on an elbow, sharp; the bark covers the fear of a man just shot by a stranger.

words.text: Hold it! Who's that?
Keep your hands where I can see 'em.

lines.speaker: sheriff
lines.trigger: You come within 25 m of him
lines.delivery: Can't lift himself; frightened, the breath short.

words.text: Who's there? Don't... don't come closer.

lines.speaker: sheriff
lines.trigger: You come within 25 m of him
lines.delivery: Head barely turned; more breath than voice.

words.text: Who... who is that?

lines.speaker: sheriff
lines.trigger: You're within 3.5 m of him, 2.5 s after the hail
lines.delivery: Knows him; relief he won't show. Flat and practical, and the question put hard.

words.text: Harlan. You're Harlan, from up the creek. I'm gut-shot. I need the doc. You going to help me or not?

lines.speaker: sheriff
lines.delivery: Asking now, not telling; the last two words a favour.

words.text: I'm shot. In the belly. Get me to the doc... will you?

lines.speaker: sheriff
lines.delivery: A whisper with one thing in it.

words.text: Doc... get me to the doc.

lines.speaker: sheriff
lines.trigger: Every 14 s you stand by him without a nod or a shake
lines.delivery: Out of patience; an order from a man used to giving them.

words.text: Well? Nod or don't, but don't just stand there.
Make up your mind, Harlan. I'm bleeding.
You deaf, man? Help me or get on.

lines.speaker: sheriff
lines.delivery: No order left in it.

words.text: Please.
Harlan... please.

lines.speaker: sheriff
lines.delivery: A breath, no words.

lines.speaker: sheriff
lines.delivery: The thanks gone in a breath; straight to orders.

words.text: Thank God. Press on it. Hard. It won't quit bleeding.

lines.speaker: sheriff
lines.delivery: Two words of order, a breath between.

words.text: Press on it... hard.

lines.speaker: sheriff
lines.delivery: Barely there.

words.text: ...hurts.

lines.speaker: sheriff
lines.delivery: Telling it to keep his mind off the hole in him; angry at himself for being fooled.

words.text: Man in a faded red shirt. Rode up easy, like he wanted directions. Then he shot me.

lines.speaker: sheriff
lines.delivery: Getting it out before it goes.

words.text: Red shirt. Faded red. Rode up like a friend.

lines.speaker: sheriff
lines.delivery: One word, all he has.

lines.speaker: sheriff
lines.delivery: Disbelief, then contempt; 'Damn you' quiet, not shouted.

words.text: You'd leave a man in the road? Then go on. Damn you.

lines.speaker: sheriff
lines.delivery: Begging, ashamed of it.

words.text: Don't... don't leave me here.

lines.speaker: sheriff
lines.delivery: A breath.

lines.speaker: sheriff
lines.trigger: Your hand first goes on his wound (hold E)
lines.delivery: A cry through the teeth, then the order steadier.

words.text: Christ! That's it. Keep on it.

lines.speaker: sheriff
lines.trigger: Your hand first goes on his wound
lines.delivery: Gasped.

words.text: ...that's it.

lines.speaker: sheriff
lines.trigger: Your hand first goes on his wound
lines.delivery: A groan.

lines.speaker: sheriff
lines.trigger: 6 s of pressure all told: packed and bound
lines.delivery: Some of the sheriff back in him; 'yonder' with a tilt of the head.

words.text: That'll hold. My horse is yonder. Get me up on him.

lines.speaker: sheriff
lines.delivery: Half a thought.

words.text: My horse...

lines.speaker: sheriff
lines.delivery: A breath.

lines.speaker: sheriff
lines.trigger: Within 10 m of him and nothing said for ~20 s
lines.delivery: Talking to keep himself here; dry even now. Each wording on its own, not a run.

words.text: Damn, it burns.
Sun's coming up. Ain't that something.
Don't you let me lie here.
Fourteen years I've rode this road. Never had to look behind me on it.
Winchester's right there on my saddle. Never put a hand to it.
words.needs: the rifle on his saddle (not built)

lines.speaker: sheriff
lines.trigger: Within 10 m of him and nothing said for ~20 s
lines.delivery: Small; a man getting cold.

words.text: I'm cold.
Don't let me lie here.
Stay where I can see you.

lines.speaker: sheriff
lines.trigger: You walk 45 m off once you've found him: you've left him
lines.delivery: Shouted after you down the road, the second one breaking.

words.text: Harlan! HARLAN!

lines.speaker: sheriff
lines.delivery: Called, but it doesn't carry.

words.text: Harlan...

lines.speaker: sheriff
lines.delivery: A breath.

scenes.title: Into town
scenes.setting: E by his horse: the card leads it into town (leading a horse isn't built). The doctor meets you at his lot; what he says first follows the sheriff's state, then your care (sheriff.care).

lines.speaker: doctor
lines.trigger: You arrive at the doctor's lot
lines.delivery: Down his steps at a walk, already rolling a sleeve; no fuss.

words.text: Gut-shot. Help me get him up the steps.

lines.speaker: doctor
lines.trigger: You arrive at the doctor's lot
lines.delivery: The same calm, a notch faster.

words.text: He's bled a fair bit. Up the steps with him, quick now.

lines.speaker: doctor
lines.trigger: You arrive at the doctor's lot
lines.delivery: 'Lord' under his breath; then plain orders.

words.text: Lord. He's near bled white. Get him inside.

lines.speaker: doctor
lines.trigger: You arrive at the doctor's lot
lines.delivery: No calm to spare; the 'Now' an order.

words.text: He's out cold. Help me with him. Now.

lines.speaker: doctor
lines.trigger: After he's looked at the wound
lines.delivery: Professional respect, said to the wound more than to you; dry.

words.text: Somebody packed that wound, and packed it right. That's bought him some hours. Come back tonight.

lines.speaker: doctor
lines.trigger: A beat after doctor_after, looking at your hands
lines.delivery: The question half asked; he sees the answer in your face and stops himself.

words.text: You've done this before. Where? ... No. Keep it.

lines.speaker: doctor
lines.trigger: After he's looked at the wound
lines.delivery: Not blaming you; telling you.

words.text: He's lost more than he can spare. I'll do what I can. It may not be much.

lines.speaker: livery
lines.trigger: The sheriff's horse is put up at the livery's front (built; no livery man yet)
lines.when: you brought him in (good or poor)
lines.delivery: Takes the reins without being asked; grumbles so he won't have to say he minds.

words.text: That's the sheriff's bay. Lord. I'll put him up. Saddle, rifle and all.
Leave him with me. I'll see he's fed, whoever's paying.

scenes.title: If you left him
scenes.setting: Built as a card: a freighter coming down the East Road finds him and hauls him into town in his wagon. These lines are for when there's a freighter in town to say it (the card stands in now).

lines.speaker: freighter
lines.trigger: You're in town after leaving him: the freighter by his wagon at the doctor's, or retelling it in the street
lines.delivery: Telling it to whoever will listen; can't stop telling it.

words.text: Found him in the road east of the ford. Talked about a red shirt the whole way in.
Red shirt, he kept saying. Red shirt, and a name. Harlan, or near it.
words.note: how the truth of 'left him' can reach the widow later (D)

lines.speaker: doctor
lines.trigger: You come to the doctor's that day
lines.delivery: Counting the hours, and not asking where you were.

words.text: A freighter brought him in at ten, insensible in the back of the wagon. He's sinking.

scenes.title: That evening, at the doctor's
scenes.setting: 'Come back tonight.' The doctor tells Harlan the sheriff will die (Sean's inventory, D). The sheriff's wife is with him.

lines.speaker: doctor
lines.trigger: You come back to the doctor's that evening
lines.delivery: Wiping his hands; the facts in order, no softening and no drama.

words.text: The ball's in the bowel. I can't get at it, and it would make no odds if I could. He'll not see another night.

lines.speaker: doctor
lines.trigger: You come back to the doctor's that evening
lines.delivery: Lower; the morphia is the only kindness left.

words.text: He's sinking. I've given him morphia. Tomorrow, I think, and it won't be easy.

lines.speaker: doctor
lines.delivery: Sending you off gently.

words.text: His wife's with him. There's nothing for you to do here tonight.
Go on. He'll ask for you in the morning.

scenes.title: Day 2: the doctor's
scenes.setting: He dies at the doctor's, his wife there. His last words follow day 1's care: clear if you packed it (care good), fading if not (poor or left). He swears Harlan in and gives him his revolver; a shake gets 'That's not the way this works, son.' He's the county sheriff; the doctor is the coroner, so the acting sheriff, and keeps Harlan on until the county names a man (C12 a).

lines.speaker: doctor
lines.trigger: You come to the doctor's on day 2
lines.delivery: At the door, low so the room won't hear.

words.text: He's asking for you. He's clear this morning. It won't last.

lines.speaker: doctor
lines.trigger: You come to the doctor's on day 2
lines.delivery: At the door, low.

words.text: He's asking for you. He comes and goes. Be quick.

lines.speaker: doctor
lines.trigger: You come to the doctor's on day 2
lines.delivery: Looking at you a moment too long.

words.text: He's been asking for you since the freighter brought him. I couldn't tell you why.

lines.speaker: widow
lines.delivery: From the chair by the bed, without getting up; level, not soft.

words.text: Were you with him?

lines.speaker: widow
lines.delivery: Plain thanks; she won't cry in front of you.

words.text: He said it was you that brought him. I'm obliged to you, Mr. Harlan.

lines.speaker: widow
lines.delivery: Flat; she's heard the town's story and is watching your face.

words.text: A freighter brought him, they tell me.

lines.speaker: sheriff
lines.delivery: Quiet and exact, spending his breath carefully.

words.text: Faded red shirt. I'd know him again. You find him, Harlan.

lines.speaker: sheriff
lines.delivery: Clutching at your sleeve; the words come apart.

words.text: ...red shirt... rode up easy...

lines.speaker: sheriff
lines.delivery: His eyes going to his wife; said to Harlan so she won't have to answer it.

words.text: He's wanted my ditch since the day I cut it. Now he'll go at her. Look to them.

lines.speaker: sheriff
lines.delivery: A word at a time.

words.text: ...the ditch... look to them...

lines.speaker: sheriff
lines.delivery: The sheriff once more: an oath given flat, like a man who's given it before. Waits for your nod.

words.text: Doc. My badge. ... Raise your hand, Harlan. You'll keep the peace of this county, best you're able. Nod, then.

lines.speaker: sheriff
lines.delivery: Pressing the badge on you because he can't say more.

words.text: Badge... Doc. Pin it on him.

lines.speaker: sheriff
lines.delivery: Brief, settled; a weight off.

words.text: Good. You're my deputy. Doc, you heard him.

lines.speaker: sheriff
lines.delivery: A breath with the word in it.

words.text: ...good.

lines.speaker: sheriff
lines.delivery: Not angry: patient, nearly a smile. Then the order.

words.text: That's not the way this works, son. ... Doc. Pin it on him.

lines.speaker: sheriff
lines.delivery: The same words with the breath run out.

words.text: ...not how it works... son.

lines.speaker: sheriff
lines.delivery: The last practical thing; dry to the end.

words.text: Take my pistol. She pulls a hair to the left.

lines.speaker: sheriff
lines.delivery: Pushing it toward you.

words.text: ...pistol... take it.

lines.speaker: sheriff
lines.delivery: Looking at the window; the road's line again, quieter.

words.text: Sun's up. Ain't that something.

lines.speaker: sheriff
lines.delivery: A word that means something to him and nothing yet to you.

words.text: ...boot.

lines.note: S33 is P, not picked: keep or cut

lines.speaker: doctor
lines.trigger: He takes bad; the doctor has you hold him while he works
lines.when: sheriff.care poor or left (S38's plant for those who didn't pack it)
lines.delivery: Working, short; then the question half asked, and dropped.

words.text: Hold him. No... yes, like that. You've done this before. Where? ... No. Keep it.

lines.speaker: doctor
lines.delivery: Two words, to the wife first.

words.text: He's gone.
He's gone, ma'am.

lines.speaker: doctor
lines.delivery: Not pleased about any of it; stating how things stand.

words.text: I'm the coroner, Harlan, so until the county sends a man I'm what law there is. And you're my deputy. Keep the badge on.

lines.speaker: widow
lines.delivery: Already folding the blanket back; dismissing you both.

words.text: I'll sit with him now. Go on, the both of you.
